scope: Current-content review against bounded guidance; not a reconstruction of all historical upstream edits. HTML shells were checked with official documentation data and remain held. No broad normalization or global review-clock reset.

records.finding: ADK still separates framework, language, runtime, evaluation, and deployment choices. The overview does not establish a working installed system.
ADK safety still distinguishes validation callbacks and runner-level security plugins; suggested integrations do not authorize enabling services or tool access.
Session history, session state, and longer-lived memory remain separate concepts; in-memory examples do not establish durable retention or tenant isolation.
The specification retains named SKILL.md frontmatter, descriptions, optional metadata, and on-demand references; experimental tool declarations are not portable authority grants.
The managed agent overview describes sandboxed execution, scoped external tools, and token/tool-based billing; it does not qualify local CLI behavior or authorize spend.
The latest-model guide is mutable and now describes Gemini 4 Argon. Exact runtime model discovery remains required; a documentation model name is not an installed-client receipt.

Headless permission denials can coexist with an apparently successful terminal result. Per-request marker availability differed; hold this fingerprint and preserve the distinction between outcome and exit status.
The decoded skills guide documents descriptions, workspace/global discovery, and plugin skills. It does not establish an observed explicit-only control on this installed version.
Apple documentation data identifies ModelActor as providing mutually exclusive model access. The pinned HTML is only a renderer shell; hold until the content-binding gap is separately repaired.
Apple documentation data describes model/view separation and Observation dependencies. The pinned HTML is only a renderer shell; hold until content-binding repair.
Apple documentation data distinguishes XCTest and Testing modules and supports incremental migration. The pinned HTML is only a renderer shell; hold until content-binding repair.
Terraform remains a declarative language for resources and dependencies. Language documentation does not grant plan execution, state mutation, or apply authority.
The official Agents CLI announcement spans scaffolding, evaluation, and deployment. Product features do not authorize running that CLI, buying inference, or creating cloud resources.
The migration announcement explicitly distinguishes Antigravity from legacy Gemini CLI and warns of incomplete parity. Keep licensing, distribution, and observed receiving behavior separate.
Data Agent Kit describes editor and coding-agent integrations across data services. Availability does not establish local installation or permission to query, execute jobs, or deploy.
Agent Platform separates development, runtime, tools, evaluation, and governance. Framework support does not establish deployed-agent acceptance or replace scoped authorization.
GitHub retains comment, approval, and requested-change review states. A review is separate from permission or readiness to merge.
The mutable Python index now identifies Python 3.15.0. Continue discovering repository interpreter and dependency versions rather than adopting the newest documentation version.
Unittest retains assertion, fixture, discovery, and asynchronous testing interfaces. Use the project interpreter; current documentation does not prove an executed test.
Spring Boot lists multiple stable, preview, and snapshot trains. Wrapper, JVM, and dependency evidence must select applicable behavior; do not infer a project upgrade.
The agentic initiative describes agent-specific security risks. Repeated body/normalized markers differed; preserve the source hold rather than masking content churn.
The retrieval-risk page addresses permission-aware stores, cross-context leakage, poisoning, and source conflicts. Normalized markers differed across samples; retain the hold.
Git merge preserves distinct merge behavior, conflict handling, and ancestry choices. A merge operation remains separately authorized; do not replace an ancestry-preserving merge with squash.
Git worktree documents linked checkout state, branch use, locks, and recovery. Protect dirty and ambiguous checkouts; isolation is not disposal authority.
The Go index covers modules, testing, diagnostics, concurrency, and database access. Discover the module toolchain and local gates instead of assuming one universal command.
OpenAI subagent guidance distinguishes roles, inherited context, configuration, and tool scope. It neither guarantees context isolation nor authorizes delegation in this task.
The .NET index provides versioned platform and framework guidance. Repository SDK, target framework, and build wrappers remain the authority for exact checks.
Next.js agent guidance now includes additional migration workflows. Do not import those skills or enable framework features; discover the installed Next.js version and requested scope.
Next.js authentication guidance retains server-side session and role checks, data access boundaries, and safe client projections. UI visibility and cached shells are not authorization controls.
OpenTelemetry separates traces, metrics, logs, and propagated context. Instrumentation availability does not prove operational coverage or acceptable cardinality.
The ASVS URL redirects to the official project page, which identifies version 5.0.0 and version-sensitive requirement identifiers. Preserve versioned mappings and avoid compliance claims.
React distinguishes derived render data and user events from Effects for external synchronization. Measure the actual interaction and retain race/cleanup concerns; avoid blanket optimization.
The versioned SLSA page describes verifiable provenance and links its predicate definition. The index does not independently verify a build level or artifact origin.
The SRE chapter distinguishes user-visible monitoring, alerting, and diagnostic detail. Signals do not by themselves prove release readiness or runtime success.
The postmortem chapter focuses on contributing conditions, impact, response, and blameless learning. A documented review is not evidence that follow-up changes worked.
Trailhead describes multitenant limits, transactional data access, and testing. Discovery of Apex APIs does not authorize anonymous execution or changing shared records.
The legacy CLI plugin URL returns an insufficient page for review. Hold its pin; use the separately reviewed combined plugin guide for current packaging discovery.
The combined plugin guide describes manifests, component directories, native lifecycle commands, and synchronization. Those documented capabilities require separate installed-version observations.
The SDK guide describes a separate stateful harness and tool policies. Samples varied, so retain this fingerprint hold; no SDK runtime or model use was tested.
The PostgreSQL current index spans SQL, server operations, transactions, and testing. Discover server version and mutation authority; the current index does not identify a deployment.
The Swift URL provides only a redirect/shell; official documentation data was read separately. Retain this pin until the reviewed content has a meaningful binding.
The decoded Swift Evolution page distinguishes reviewed proposals from installed language behavior. Compiler version, language mode, and enabled features remain required evidence.
The TypeScript index covers compiler configuration, module interoperability, and declaration files. Current release notes do not establish a project compiler version or safe upgrade.

additional_reviews.finding: The page retains incremental filtering, grain and unique-key contracts, null/duplicate-key risks, schema-change limits, and full-refresh consequences. It also describes adapter-specific compatibility constraints. Existing guidance requires discovering exact adapter versions and reviewing those contracts; no warehouse execution or automatic upgrade is authorized.
